question: In any tennis game, if both players win three points each in a game (i.e. score is 40-40), then it's called a __________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**deuce**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In tennis, a score of 40-40 is referred to as a **deuce**.
 
• When the score reaches deuce, a player must win two consecutive points to win the game.
 
• The first point won after deuce is called "advantage." If the player with the advantage wins the next point, they win the game; if they lose it, the score returns to deuce.
 
• This rule ensures that a player must lead by two points to secure a game after reaching deuce.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The term **"deuce"** is derived from the Old French word "deus" meaning two, indicating that two more points are needed to win the game from this score.
 
• Tennis scoring can trace its origins back to medieval France, and the unique terms and scoring system have been retained over centuries.
 
• Understanding the concept of deuce is fundamental for anyone learning the rules and structure of tennis matches.
